root.name: Semi-Slav Defense: Rubinstein System
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c6 4. Nf3 Nf6 5. e3 Nbd7 6. Ne5

overview: After 5...Nbd7 White plays 6.Ne5, an early central knight aimed at the Black knight and f7, instead of the Meran 6.Bd3. Black usually plays ...Bd6 and ...O-O or trades on e5, while White follows with f4 and a kingside build-up. It is a combative anti-Meran with a strategic flavour. I am not fully sure of this name and move order.

white_ideas.idea: Plant the knight on e5 and support it with f4
Develop Bd3, Qf3 or Qc2, and castle

black_ideas.idea: Trade the knight with ...Nxe5 or hit it with ...Bd6

typical_structures.structure: White knight on e5 supported by f4
Semi-Slav centre with pawns on c6, d5, e6

character.notes: White has an early plan; Black has a solid structure but the play is combative.

structure.notes: The d4/c4 and d5/e6 pawns are in tension.

approach.notes: A respected branch of the Semi-Slav.

level.notes: Needs both theory and plan understanding.

character.reason: Combative but not as forcing as the Botvinnik.

plans.reason: White places a knight on e5.
